人.noteEn: Pictograph of the side view of a person.

手.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand with five fingers.

足.noteEn: Pictograph of a foot attached to a leg.

男.noteEn: Traditionally males (男) were the people who plowed (力) the fields (田).

子.noteEn: Pictograph of a small child with its two arms outstretched.

生.noteEn: Pictograph of a sprout emerging from the ground.

先.noteEn: Depicts a person (人) stepping forward (止) leading the way.

本.noteEn: Addition of a horizontal line toward the bottom of 木 (tree) to represent the roots of the tree.

大.noteEn: Pictograph of a person with outstretched arms, representing the meaning "big".

小.noteEn: Pictograph of three small dots, representing grains of sand or rice, to convey the meaning "small".

中.noteEn: A line passing through the middle of a box, representing the meaning "middle".

上.noteEn: Originally a small line or dot above a longer line, indicating "up". The vertical line was added to distinguish the character from 二 (two).

下.noteEn: Originally a small line or dot below a longer line, indicating "down". The vertical line was added to distinguish the character from 二 (two).

左.noteEn: Pictograph of a left hand. The 工 (work) component was added later to represent the meaning "help; assist", now written as 佐.

一.noteEn: A single horizontal stroke, representing the number one.

二.noteEn: Two horizontal strokes, representing the number two.

三.noteEn: Three horizontal strokes, representing the number three.

分.noteEn: Depicts a knife ( 刀 ) being used to cut two things apart (八).

半.noteEn: Depicts cutting a cow (牛) into two halves (八).

来.noteEn: Pictograph of wheat. The current meaning "come" is a phonetic loan. The original meaning "wheat" is now written as 麥.

見.noteEn: Pictograph of a person (卩) using their eye (目) to see (見).

休.noteEn: Depicts a person (亻) leaning on a tree (木) to rest (休).

天.noteEn: Pictograph of a line above a person, representing the sky.

雨.noteEn: Pictograph of rain falling from a cloud.

電.noteEn: Depicts lightning (电) during a rainstorm (雨).

白.noteEn: Origin unclear. Used in ancient texts to mean "white" and "hundred" (百).

夏.noteEn: Pictograph of a person, represented by their head (頁) and feet (夂), being heated underneath the sun (日). The sun component was later omitted for brevity during the Warring States period.

朝.noteEn: Depicts the early part of morning when the sun (日) can still be seen on the horizon between blades of grass (屮), and the moon (月) is still in the sky.

旅.noteEn: Pictograph of soldiers marching beneath a flag. The original meaning was "army brigade", but later shifted to "travel".

使.noteEn: The characters 史 (history), 吏 (government official), 使 (cause; use; instruct), and 事 (matter; work; affair) are all etymologically related and all derive from the same ancient character, depicting a hand (又) holding some object. There are various theories about theories about what this object is, including a writing utensil, a container for official documents, a flag, or a hunting tool. These four characters were originally all written the same, but later marks were added to distinguish them.

長.noteEn: Pictograph of a person with long hair.

出.noteEn: Pictograph of a foot (止) going out of an enclosure.

高.noteEn: Pictograph of a tall building. Similar to 京.

午.noteEn: Pictograph of a pestle used for pounding rice, now written as 杵. The current meaning "noon" is a phonetic loan.

名.noteEn: Traditionally explained as identifying youself at night (夕) by saying (口) your name (名) because is too dark for others to see you.

無.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of a person (大) dancing with ornamental leather hides (革) hanging from his arms, conveying the meaning "dance". Later, two feet (舛) were added to the bottom of the character to form 舞 (dance), and 無 was borrowed for its sound to represent the meaning "not".

母.noteEn: Pictograph of a woman kneeling, with two dots representing the two nipples that mothers use to feed their young.

友.noteEn: Pictograph of two hands togther to convey the meaning "friend".

父.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand holding something. There are various theories about what the object being held is, including a hatchet (now written as 斧), or a rod.

丈.noteEn: Depicts 10 (十) hand-lengths (又): 丈 is a traditional Chinese unit of length equivalent to about 3 meters.

事.noteEn: The characters 史 (history), 吏 (government official), 使 (cause; use; instruct), and 事 (matter; work; affair) are all etymologically related and all derive from the same ancient character, depicting a hand (又) holding some object. There are various theories about theories about what this object is, including a writing utensil, a container for official documents, a flag, or a hunting tool. These four characters were originally all written the same, but later marks were added to distinguish them.

自.noteEn: Pictograph of a nose. Original form of 鼻 (nose). In China, when people point to themselves, they typically point to their nose.

社.noteEn: Originally depicted a god (礻) of the land (土). The meaning later shifted to "society".

発.noteEn: Depicts a person standing on their two feet, pulling back a bowstring, about to shoot an arrow. Conveys the meaning "shoot; send out".

員.noteEn: Depicts the round opening (口) of a cooking pot (鼎). Based on the original meaning "round", now written as 圓. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

立.noteEn: Pictograph of a person standing on the ground.

開.noteEn: Pictograph of two hands opening the bolt on a door.

言.noteEn: Pictograph of a tongue sticking out of a mouth. In old scripts written the same as 舌 but with an extra line.

主.noteEn: Pictograph of a torch, now written as 炷. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

不.noteEn: Pictograph of sepals of a flower. The meaning "no" is a phonetic loan.

公.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of a vessel for holding liquid. The original meaning is now written as 瓮, with the 瓦 (pottery) component added at the bottom. The current meaning "public" is a phonetic loan.

世.noteEn: Three copies of 十 (ten) to make 30, similar to the archaic character 卅 (30). Conveys the meaning "30-year generation", also symbolizing a branching family tree.

安.noteEn: Variously explained as (1) a woman is what makes a home feel peaceful, or (2) a woman feels safe under the shelter of a roof.

元.noteEn: Pictograph of a person with two lines added at the head area, representing the meaning the meaning "head" or "first".

重.noteEn: Pictograph of a person (亻) carrying a heavy basket (東).

画.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand holding a writing utensil (聿) and drawing something.

別.noteEn: Pictograph depicting cutting meat off of a bone.

品.noteEn: Triple of 口. Depicts a variety of utensils together.

死.noteEn: Depicts the carcass (歹) of a person (人).

有.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand holding meat

少.noteEn: Pictograph of four small dots, representing grains of sand or rice, to convey the meaning "less". Similar to 小.

料.noteEn: Depicts a dipper (斗) full of rice (米).

建.noteEn: Depicts the process of setting something up. The 聿 component here is used to depict a hand holding up a wooden post, rather than a writing utensil.

止.noteEn: Pictograph of a foot. The meaning of this character has shifted over time and now means "stop".

送.noteEn: Depicts walking (辶) while carrying a present in both hands.

族.noteEn: Depicts a flag (㫃) representing a clan and an arrow (矢) representing their military power.

去.noteEn: Origin unclear. The 口 component is variously explained as (1) an opening to a building or cave that the person is departing from, or (2) an anus, i.e. the orifice through which things leave a person.

音.noteEn: Pictograph of sound (represented with one or two horizontal lines) coming from a tongue (舌). In seal script, identical to 言 (speech) except with a dot or line added to the middle of the 口 (mouth) component.

図.noteEn: Pictograph of a map of territory.

歩.noteEn: Pictograph of one foot in front of another, depicting footsteps.

風.noteEn: Originally written the same as 鳳 (phoenix) because the two characters sounded the same. Later the bottom part of the character was abbreviated to distinguish the two characters.

走.noteEn: Pictograph of a person swaying their arms while walking.

夕.noteEn: Pictograph of the moon. Used to express "evening" or "night".

肉.noteEn: Pictograph of a piece of meat.

堂.noteEn: Pictograph large room or platform rising from the ground.

弟.noteEn: Pictograph of a rope wrapped around a weapon. Relation to current meaning "younger brother" unclear.

牛.noteEn: Pictograph of the head of a cow.

兄.noteEn: Pictograph of a mouth on top of a person, representing an older brother giving orders.

民.noteEn: Pictograph of a line going into the eye. Relation to current meaning unclear.

連.noteEn: Depicts a line of man-drawn (辶) carriages (車).

対.noteEn: Origin unclear. Appears to be a hand using some sort of tool, possibly a rake or a hoe.

内.noteEn: Depicts an entrance (入) to a hall (冂).

相.noteEn: Represents an eye (目) observing a tree (木). Based on the original meaning "observe". The meaning of this character has shifted over time and now means "compare; mutual; each other".

回.noteEn: Originally a spiral, conveying the meaning "to turn around".

実.noteEn: 貫 is a pictograph of a string of money. Based on the original meaning "thrive; plentiful". The meaning later shifted to "real", "true", and "fruit".

表.noteEn: Depicts clothes (衣) made from fur (毛), typically the outermost layer of clothing. In simplified Chinese 表 is also used to mean "wristwatch", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 錶.

経.noteEn: Pictograph of a loom for weaving. In a loom threads have to pass through each other.

化.noteEn: Pictograph of a right-side up person and an upside-down person, depicting the meaning "turn around" or "transform".

首.noteEn: Pictograph of a head (hair above an eye).

要.noteEn: Pictograph of two hands grabbing a woman's waist. The current meaning "want" is a phonetic loan. The original meaning "waist" is now written as 腰.

制.noteEn: Depicts cutting down a tree (木) with a knife (刂).

取.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand (又) grabbing an ear (耳). In ancient China, the ears of opponents in battle were cut off and collected as tokens of victory.

加.noteEn: Depicts making noises with the mouth (口) while exerting strength (力). Based on the original meaning "exert strength". The meaning later shifted to "raise; increase; add"

初.noteEn: Depicts cutting out fabric (衤) with a knife (刀), the first step in making clothes.

支.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand (又) lifting a piece of bamboo (个).

報.noteEn: Pictograph of a kneeling person (卩) being forced by a hand (又) into shackles (㚔). Based on the original meaning "punish". The meaning later shifted to "revenge", "recompense", "report", and "announce".

原.noteEn: Depicts a spring (泉) originating (原) from a cliff (厂).

得.noteEn: Originally written as 㝵. Depicts a hand (寸) grabbing a shell (貝), used as currency in ancient China, to convey the meaning "get". The 彳 (movement) component was added later.

解.noteEn: Depicts separating (解) the horns (角) from a cow (牛) using a knife (刀).

交.noteEn: Pictograph of a person standing with crossed legs, conveying the meaning "to cross".

向.noteEn: Depicts a mouth (口) in a closed space (宀) making an echo sound. Based on the original meaning "echo; sound", now written as 響. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

面.noteEn: Pictograph of the outline of a face, with an eye (目) in the middle. In simplified Chinese 面 is also used to mean "noodles", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 麵.

告.noteEn: Pictograph of a tongue extending from an open mouth. Graphically similar to 舌 (tongue).

反.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand (又) climbing a cliff (厂). Based on original meaning "pull", later extended to "turn around", "oppose".

参.noteEn: Depicts three stars joined together; in Chinese astronomy 參 is a constellation of three stars. 彡 is a sound component.

利.noteEn: Depicts harvesting grain (禾) with a blade (刂). Harvest was the main source of profit in agricultural societies.

信.noteEn: Conveys trusting (信) what a person (人) says (言).

引.noteEn: Pictograph of a bowstring being pulled back.

直.noteEn: Pictograph of a straight line coming from the eye, depicting somone looking straight at something. An additional stroke was added at the bottom for unkown reasons.

両.noteEn: Combination of two 丙 characters. The significance of 丙 is unclear.

果.noteEn: Pictograph of fruit growing on a tree.

必.noteEn: Pictograph of a weapon, now written as 柲. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

争.noteEn: Pictograph of multiple hands grabbing at the same object.

能.noteEn: Pictograph of a bear holding meat in its mouth. Based on the original meaning "bear". The meaning of this character has shifted over time and now means "ability; power".

位.noteEn: Depicts a person (亻) standing (立) in a specific location.

流.noteEn: Depicts an upside-down child (子) being born headfirst with amniotic fluid flowing out.

可.noteEn: The right component is a pictograph of an axe handle, now written as 柯 (kē). 口 (mouth) was added later to indicate that the character is only "mouthed", i.e. only used for its phonetic value.

身.noteEn: Pictograph of a person with an protruding midsection. The protruding midsection is variously explained as (1) representing the main part of a person's body, or (2) as representing a pregnant woman that has a body inside her body.

付.noteEn: Depicts a hand (寸) giving payment to a person (亻).

夫.noteEn: Pictograph of a man. The top horizontal stroke is traditionally explained as a hairpin which was only worn by adults.

断.noteEn: Depicts cutting off threads with an axe (斤)

備.noteEn: Pictograph of a container for holding arrows, which helped in preparation for battle. The 亻 (person) component was added later.

害.noteEn: Pictograph of a lid over a container. Based on the original meaning "lid", now written as 蓋. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

乗.noteEn: Pictograph of a person (人) who has climbed up a tree (木).

退.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of a foot (止) retreating back to a safe place. The 辶 (walk) component was added later.

負.noteEn: Depicts a person (人) carrying money (貝) on his back.

失.noteEn: Pictograph of something falling out of the hand.

差.noteEn: Depicts grain (麥) being rolled between the fingers in the left hand (左). Based on the original meaning "rub between fingers", now written as 搓. The meaning later shifted to "uneven" and "error".

末.noteEn: Similar to 木, with an extra line at the top. Depicts the tip of a tree.

守.noteEn: Depicts a hand (寸) guarding a building (宀).

若.noteEn: Pictograph of a person smoothing out their hair with their hands. Based on the original meaning "smooth". The meaning later shifted to "obedient" and "conform to". The 口 (mouth) component was added later when the character became more abstract.

望.noteEn: Pictograph of a person standing up (𡈼) and gazing at the moon (月). 亡 is a sound component that was added later.

非.noteEn: Pictograph of two wings facing opposite directions.

段.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand holding a forging hammer (殳) and hitting a stone (石). Based on the original meaning "forge", now written as 鍛. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

良.noteEn: Pictograph of a hallway, now written as 廊. The character is based on the original meaning "hallway", which is unrelated to the modern meaning.

突.noteEn: Depicts a dog (犬) running out of a cave (穴).

光.noteEn: Pictograph of fire on top of a person.

科.noteEn: Depicts measuring out grain (禾) with a dipper (斗).

太.noteEn: Addition of a dot to 大 (dà; big) to mean "very" or "extremely".

殺.noteEn: Depicts a person being impaled in the head (杀) with a spear (殳).

単.noteEn: Pictograph of a hunting or military trap constructed from two rocks and a net. The current meaning "single" is a phonetic loan.

降.noteEn: Depicts two feet (止) descending down a hill (阝).

危.noteEn: Depicts a person (人) standing precariously on the edge of a mountain cliff (山).

具.noteEn: Depicts two hands (廾) handling a cooking pot (鼎).

因.noteEn: Pictograph of clothing surrounding (囗) a person (人), now written as 裀. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

未.noteEn: Similar to 木, with extra branches added. Based on the original meaning "tree trunk", now written as 枚. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

亡.noteEn: Pictograph of the tip of a knife blade.

王.noteEn: Pictograph of an axe head, used as a symbol of the king's military authority.

妻.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand grabbing a woman's hair. In ancient China, women of marriagable age wore hairpins (compare with 每).

散.noteEn: Depicts hitting (攵) bamboo (竹) to break it apart. The purpose of the 月 component is unclear.

静.noteEn: Both 青 and 爭 are sound components.

絶.noteEn: Depicts a knife (刀) cutting between threads (絲).

老.noteEn: Pictograph of an old person with long hair bent over and leaning on a cane.

困.noteEn: Depicts a tree (木) being surrounded (囗).

息.noteEn: Pictograph of air going into the nose (自). The lines representing breath were later reanalyzed as 心 (heart).

互.noteEn: Depicts two symmetric figures facing each other.

束.noteEn: Pictograph of a bag tied at both ends.

閉.noteEn: Depicts a door closed shut with horizontal bars.

折.noteEn: Depicts a hand (扌) cutting something off with an axe (斤).

歯.noteEn: Pictograph of a mouth full of teeth. The sound component 止 was added later.

昔.noteEn: Pictograph of the sun (日) having passed through many cycles of rising and setting.

髪.noteEn: Originally a combination of 首 (head) and 犬 (dog), both of which are hairy. Later the 首 (head) component was changed to 髟 (hairy).

才.noteEn: Pictograph of a small plant starting to emerge from the ground. Based on the original meaning "to sprout". The meaning of this character has shifted over time and now means "talent".

区.noteEn: Depicts a group of things (品) in an enclosed area.

県.noteEn: Pictograph of a severed head (首) hanging on a rope (系) from a tree (木). Based on the original meaning "hang" or "suspend". The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

各.noteEn: Pictograph of a foot (夂) entering an opening, (口), the opposite of 出 (exit). Based on the original meaning "enter", unrelated to the current meaning "each", which is a phonetic loan.

革.noteEn: Pictograph of animal hide laying flat.

比.noteEn: Pictograph of two people side-by-side, conveying the meaning "to put together", "match", or "compare".

農.noteEn: Depicts using a farming tool (辰) in a field (田) surrounded by forest (林).

州.noteEn: Pictograph of a region of dry land between two rivers.

脳.noteEn: The brain is part of the body (⺼) composed of a system of pathways (巛) located inside of the skull (囟).

専.noteEn: Depicts a hand (寸) spinning a wheel (叀). Based on the original meaning "turn", now written as 轉. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

谷.noteEn: Pictograph of the valley between two mountains.

史.noteEn: The characters 史 (history), 吏 (government official), 使 (cause; use; instruct), and 事 (matter; work; affair) are all etymologically related and all derive from the same ancient character, depicting a hand (又) holding some object. There are various theories about theories about what this object is, including a writing utensil, a container for official documents, a flag, or a hunting tool. These four characters were originally all written the same, but later marks were added to distinguish them.

兵.noteEn: Pictograph of two hands (廾) holding some sort of weapon.

丸.noteEn: Depicts something tilted or leaning forward; i.e. something that can be turned around.

周.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of engraved jade, now written as 琱. 口 (mouth) indicates that the character is only "mouthed", i.e. only used for its phonetic value. In simplified Chinese 周 is also used to mean "week", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 週.

戸.noteEn: Pictograph of a door, taken from the left half of 門.

央.noteEn: Pictograph of a person (大) with a cangue (torture device for punishing criminals) around his neck. People wearing such devices were not able to reach their mouth with their own hands, and were forced to beg for food.

競.noteEn: Pictograph of two people side-by-side competing with each other.

介.noteEn: Pictograph of a person between two lines.

将.noteEn: Depicts a hand (寸) taking a piece of meat (肉), conveying the meaning "take". 爿 (qiáng) is a sound component.

児.noteEn: Pictograph of a child with an opening in the top of its head. Represents the soft spot (fontanel) at the top of young infant heads.

印.noteEn: Pictograph of a kneeling person (卩) being held down by a hand (爪). Based on the original meaning "restrain", now written as 抑. The meaning later shifted to "push down", "stamp", and "print".

逆.noteEn: Originally written as 屰, a pictograph of an upside-down person. The 辶 (walk) component was added later.

暴.noteEn: Origin unclear. Possibly represents two hands (共) laying out rice (米) to dry under the sun (日), representing the meaning "dry out under the sun", now written as 曝.

占.noteEn: In ancient China fortune-tellers made cracks (卜) and holes (口) in turtle shells for the purpose of divination.

芸.noteEn: Originally written as 埶. The 艹 and 云 components were added later for unknown reasons.

玉.noteEn: Pictograph of a ritual object made out of several pieces of jade joined together by a string. A dot was later added to 玉 to distinguish it from 王 (king).

則.noteEn: Depicts carving inscriptions on bronzeware (鼎) with a knife (刂). Based on the original meaning "law". In ancient China, some legal writings were inscribed on bronzeware.

乱.noteEn: Pictograph of two hands doing work with tangled threads.

豊.noteEn: Pictograph of a pot floruishing with plants.

厚.noteEn: Depicts a container of wine that has been aging in a cave, thus having a strong flavor.

卒.noteEn: A cross shape (十) added to clothes (衣). Origin unclear.

承.noteEn: Pictograph of two hands carrying a person.

血.noteEn: Depicts a drop of blood in a container (皿).

季.noteEn: Based on the original meaning "young". 禾 represents short stalks of grain, 子 represents a young child.

永.noteEn: Pictograph of a long river with a tributary.

香.noteEn: Represents the sweet (甘) smell of fresh grain (禾).

巨.noteEn: Pictograph of a carpenter's square, a tool for measuring right angles. Based on the original meaning "carpenter's square", now written as 矩. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

希.noteEn: Composed of 爻 (intertwined cross shape) and 巾 (cloth). Conveys a rare type of stitched cloth, corresponding to the original meaning "sparse; rare". The meaning later shifted to "hope".

枚.noteEn: Depicts a hand (攵) holding a piece of wood (木).

骨.noteEn: Pictograph of a bone (冎) with muscle (⺼) attached to it.

包.noteEn: Pictograph of an unborn baby contained inside its mother.

弱.noteEn: Origin unclear. Contains two bows (弓) with extra marks, perhaps indicating damage or weakness in the bows.

替.noteEn: Depicts two standing people (夫) changing places.

双.noteEn: Depicts a pair of birds in the hand.

孝.noteEn: Filial piety (孝) is the respect that the young (子) must have for their elders (老).

片.noteEn: Pictograph of a slice of a tree, taken from the right half of 木 (tree).

敬.noteEn: Depicts kneeling (茍) and extending one's hands 攵 in respect.

泉.noteEn: Pictograph of water flowing out of a spring.

皮.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand (又) peeling off the skin from an animal.

祭.noteEn: Depicts a hand (又) offering meat (⺼) as a sacrifice to a deity (示).

筆.noteEn: Depicts a utensil for writing (聿) made from bamboo (⺮).

宝.noteEn: Pictograph an assortment of valuable things, including jade (玉) and shells (貝), being stored safely under a roof (宀). The 缶 component represents the sound.

兆.noteEn: Pictograph of cracks in a shell used in ancient China for fortune-telling.

祝.noteEn: Depicts a kneeling person (卩) opening their mouth (口) to offer good wishes. The 礻 component is often used in abstract/spiritual characters.

寿.noteEn: The top component is a remnant of 老 (old). The origin of the bottom component is unclear.

甘.noteEn: Pictograph of something sweet inside the mouth (口).

臣.noteEn: Pictograph of an eye, similar to 目. Based on the original meaning "to glare at", now written as 瞋. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

冊.noteEn: Pictograph of strips of bamboo strung together. In ancient China writing was done on bamboo strips.

刷.noteEn: The left component is a pictograph of a brush. The 刂 (knife) component indicates that it is a tool/utensil.

孫.noteEn: Semantic compound of child (子) and 系 (relation; connection).

毒.noteEn: Depicts a plant (屮) that is wicked (毐), i.e. a poisonous plant.

拝.noteEn: Depicts two hands put (手) together as a sign of respect.

乾.noteEn: 倝 is used to represent the sound. The purpose of the 乙 component is unclear.

辛.noteEn: Pictograph of a chisel-like tool used to tattoo the face of criminals as punishment (see 黑).

麦.noteEn: The top component 來 is a pictograph of wheat. It is unclear why the foot component (夂) was added to the character for "wheat".

胃.noteEn: The top component is a pictograph of the stomach. The bottom component ⺼ (flesh) is a common component in body parts.

灰.noteEn: After a fire (火) burns down, the left over ash (灰) can be touched with the hands (又).

貝.noteEn: Pictograph of a cowrie shell. In ancient China such shells were used as currency.

皿.noteEn: Pictograph of a container for holding food.

瓦.noteEn: Pictograph of a tool for making pottery.

爪.noteEn: Pictograph of an animal paw. Usually means "hand" when used as a component in other characters.

斬.noteEn: Beheading is a military action (車 - chariot) performed with an axe (斤).

塞.noteEn: Depicts two hands (廾) stuffing various objects (工) into an enclosed space (宀) and sealing it with clay (土).

巾.noteEn: Pictograph of a cloth hanging downwards.

氏.noteEn: Pictograph of a man bowing down.

保.noteEn: Pictograph of a person carrying a child on their back.

派.noteEn: Pictograph of a split in a river.

企.noteEn: Depicts a person (人) standing on their feet (止).

幹.noteEn: Both 倝 and 干 serve as sound components.

宮.noteEn: Pictograph of a building with two floors.

率.noteEn: Pictograph of a rope (系) surrounded by four dots. Originally depicted a type of rope. The meaning later shifted to "lead".

衛.noteEn: Depicts feet (止) walking around, patrolling a street intersection (行).

監.noteEn: Pictograph of a person leaning over to look at his own reflection on a plate.

撃.noteEn: Depicts a hand (手) hitting something with a spear (殳).

士.noteEn: Pictograph of the head of an axe. Likely used to represent a military officer.

討.noteEn: Depicts using speech (言) and one's hands (寸) to ask for something.

及.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand (又) reaching to grab a person (人).

系.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand (又) holding a group of threads (糸) that are connected together (系).

従.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of one person following another (从). Later the 彳 and 止 components were added to indicate movement.

異.noteEn: Pictograph of a person with an unusual head.

素.noteEn: Depicts raw silk (糸). The significance of the top component is unclear.

益.noteEn: Depicts food or drink filling up a container (皿). Based on the original meaning "overflow", now written as 溢. The meaning later shifted to "increase" and "benefit".

皇.noteEn: Depicts a decorative crown above 王 (king).

興.noteEn: Depicts four hands (舁) working together (同) to raise something.

継.noteEn: Depicts a continuous series of silk (糸) threads (絲).

葬.noteEn: Depicts a dead body being buried beneath the grass.

司.noteEn: 司 (take charge) and its mirror image 后 (empress) were originally used interchangeably. The origin of both characters is unclear.

執.noteEn: Pictograph of a person with hands (丮) bound by shackles (㚔).

陣.noteEn: Depicts a group (阝) of soldiers in chariots (車).

我.noteEn: Pictograph of a weapon or farming tool with a forked blade and long handle. The meaning "I; me" is a phonetic loan.

秀.noteEn: Based on the original meaning "to blossom/bloom". The 禾 (plant) component depicts a blossoming plant. The purpose of the bottom 乃 component is unclear.

尾.noteEn: Depicts fur (毛) protruding from the posterior of an animal.

棄.noteEn: Pictograph of two hands (廾) putting a child (子) in a basket (其) for the purpose of abandoning or disposing with it.

需.noteEn: Originally was a pictograph of a person standing under the rain (雨), representing the meaning "to get wet", now written as 濡. The current meaning is a phonetic loan. The person component was later replaced with the phonetic component 而. Due to historical phonetic shifts, 需 and 而 no longer sound similar.

射.noteEn: Depicts a hand pulling back a bowstring with an arrow to shoot.

貴.noteEn: Pictograph of two hands carrying a shell. (Shells were used in ancient china as currency.)

焦.noteEn: Combination of 隹 (bird) and 灬 (fire). The purpose of the 隹 component is unclear.

災.noteEn: Depicts a fire (火) burning a building (宀).

至.noteEn: Pictograph of an arrow hitting its target.

宗.noteEn: Depicts a spiritual (示) edifice (宀), such as an ancestral shrine.

典.noteEn: Depicts a book (冊) on a table.

戒.noteEn: Depicts two hands (廾) holding a weapon (戈) guarding against danger.

免.noteEn: Pictograph of a person with a hat, now written as 冕. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

華.noteEn: Pictograph of a flower. Originally used to mean "flower", now written as 花. The meaning later shifted to "blossoming", "flourishing" and "magnificent". The 艹 (grass) component was added in Seal script.

徳.noteEn: Depicts walking (彳) through life with a straight (直) heart (心) to represent the meaning "virtue". 直 also serves as a phonetic component.

里.noteEn: A village (里) is an area of land (土) where people have fields (田). In simplified Chinese 里 is also used to mean "inside", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 裡.

威.noteEn: 戌 is a pictograph of an axe, representing military power. 女 possibly alludes to the domestic power wielded by mothers-in-law in ancient China.

熊.noteEn: Pictograph of a bear holding meat in its mouth. Based on 能, with four dots added at the bottom to differentiate it, representing four legs.

倉.noteEn: Depicts things being stored together (合) behind a door (戶).

索.noteEn: Pictograph of two hands (廾) twisting together a long rope (糸).

兼.noteEn: Depicts a hand (又) holding two stalks of grain (禾).

旨.noteEn: Depicts a spoon (匕) going into the mouth (口), conveying the original meaning "delicious".

即.noteEn: Depicts a kneeling person (卩) approaching a vessel of food (皀). Based on the original meaning "come to eat", which later shifted to "approach", "be near", and "be the same".

竜.noteEn: Pictograph of a dragon curled up.

斉.noteEn: Pictograph of stalks of millet. Possibly alludes to the even and uniform appearance of a millet field.

尽.noteEn: Pictograph of scrubbing dishes clean after one is finished eating.

帝.noteEn: Pictograph of firewood arranged together for the purpose of an imperial ancestral sacrifice.

丁.noteEn: Pictograph of a nail, which is now written as 釘.

冒.noteEn: Pictograph of a hat over an eye. Old way of writing 帽 (hat).

之.noteEn: Pictograph of a foot, phonetically and visually similar to 止, which also a pictograph of a foot.

曽.noteEn: Pictograph of a cooking pot. Based on the original meaning "cauldron; cooking pot", now written as 甑. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

陳.noteEn: Originally written as 陣. The 車 (chariot) component was changed to 東 (east) to distinguish the two characters.

克.noteEn: Pictograph of a person (人) carrying a heavy weight on their back.

須.noteEn: Pictograph of a person with a bearded face. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

卓.noteEn: Pictograph of a person standing erect with something above the head. The significance of the object above the head is unclear.

穴.noteEn: Pictograph of an opening to a cave.

昌.noteEn: Duplication of the 日 (sun) character, meaning "sunlight". The meaning later shifted to "beautiful" and "flourishing".

没.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand reaching in the water to grab something. Later the meaning shifted to "drown". This meaning is only used when the character is pronouned "mò". When pronounced "méi" (which is much more common), it means "not have". This meaning is a phonetic loan, unrelated to the original meaning.

尋.noteEn: Pictograph of two outstretched arms searching for something.

豆.noteEn: Pictograph of a stemmed bowl. Current meaning is a phonetic loan.

准.noteEn: Simplified form of 準. Phonosemantic compound. 氵 represents the meaning and 隼 represents the sound. The 氵 (water) component is used because level tools that ensure flatness take advantage of water having a flat surface.

雷.noteEn: Depicts rain (雨) and lightning (申) together.

亜.noteEn: Originally depicted a common Chinese architectural shape. Relation to current meaning unclear.

獄.noteEn: Depicts being between two barking (言) guard dogs (犬).

尚.noteEn: Pictograph of a large room or platform.

顕.noteEn: Depicts the head of a person (頁) looking carefully at small threads (絲) which are made visible by the sun (日).

粛.noteEn: The 𣶒 (deep; profound) component hints at the meaning. The purpose of the 聿 (writing utensil) component is unclear.

鬼.noteEn: Pictograph of a human-like being with an unnatural head and a tail.

庶.noteEn: Depicts a stone pot (石) over a fire (灬). Based on the original meaning "to cook; boil", now written as 煮. The current meaning is a phonetic loan. 石 also serves as a sound component.

呈.noteEn: Depicts speaking (口) to an authority (王).

后.noteEn: 后 (empress) and its mirror image 司 (take charge) were originally used interchangeably. The origin of both characters is unclear. In simplified Chinese 后 is also used to mean "after, behind", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 後.

琴.noteEn: The top component is a pictograph of a zither-like stringed musical instrument. 今 is a sound component.

班.noteEn: Depicts a knife (刂) cutting a gem into two halves (玨), based on the original meaning "to divide". The meaning later shifted to "division", "group", and "team".

辰.noteEn: Pictograph of an ancient farming tool.

憂.noteEn: Originally composed of 頁 (head) and 又 (hand), depicting covering one's face in sorrow. The semantic 心 (heart) component was added later.

乏.noteEn: Line over 之 (foot), similar to how 正 (straight; correct) is a line over 止 (foot). Possibly represents the opposite of 正, since the top line in 乏 is written in the opposite direction as the top line in 正.

寸.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand with a line marking a spot on the wrist. In traditional Chinese medicine this spot on the wrist where the pulse can be taken is called the 寸口.

凶.noteEn: Pictograph of a trap in the ground.

賓.noteEn: Depicts someone walking (止) into a house (宀) with a gift (貝).

庄.noteEn: Simplified form of 莊. Phonosemantic compound. 艹 represents the meaning and 壯 represents the sound.

苗.noteEn: Sprouts are plants (艹) that rise from the field (田).

亘.noteEn: Simplified form of 亙. Pictograph of continuously revolving circle.

呉.noteEn: Pictograph of a person (大) standing up, yelling with an open mouth (口).

凡.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of a plate or dish. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

麗.noteEn: Pictograph of a deer (鹿) with two beautiful antlers.

刃.noteEn: Pictograph of a knife. Similar to 刀 (knife), with an added dot.

宜.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of two pieces of meat (肉) on a table. Based on the original meaning "delicacy" or "fine food". The meaning later shifted to "proper".

朱.noteEn: Based on the original meaning "tree trunk", now written as 株. Derivative of 木 (tree). The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

舌.noteEn: Pictograph of a tongue sticking out of a mouth, with a splatter of spit at the end.

羅.noteEn: Depicts a net (网) for catching birds (隹). The 糹 (silk; thread) component was added later.

羊.noteEn: Pictograph of the horns on a sheep.

又.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand. The character is based on the original meaning "right hand", which is unrelated to the modern meaning.

斗.noteEn: Pictograph of a cup or dipper. In simplified Chinese 斗 is also used to mean "fight, struggle", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 鬥.

肖.noteEn: Depicts the moon (月) getting smaller (小) and disappearing as part of the lunar cycle. Based on the original meaning "decrease; disappear", now written as 消. The meaning later shifted to "resemble; similar".

享.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of a temple or a shrine. The meaning later shifted to "festive" and "enjoy".

奴.noteEn: Depicts a hand behind a woman slave's back forcing her to work.

喬.noteEn: Originally written the same as 高 (tall). The 大 component was added to distinguish the two characters.

寅.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of an arrow (矢). Later two hand components (爪) were added on the sides.

曹.noteEn: Depicts a pair of baskets (東). Based on the original meaning "pair". Later the meaning shifted to "of the same generation". The purpose of the additional 口 (mouth) component is unclear.

卑.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand holding the base of an object.

帥.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of two hands pulling a rod, based on the original meaning "lead; command". The meaning later shifted to "handsome". The purpose of the 巾 (cloth) is unclear. It possibly represents a special cloth worn by commanders.

朋.noteEn: Pictograph of two strings of objects mounted together. Originally meant "pair", later the meaning shifted to "friend". The modern form is visually similar to 月 (moon) but the meaning is not related.

臼.noteEn: Pictograph of a mortar: a hollow vessel used to crush ingredients.

巽.noteEn: Depicts two people kneeling (卩) together in obedience.

升.noteEn: Pictograph of a spoon, a utensil used to pick things up.

巴.noteEn: Pictograph of a person grabbing something with their hand.

某.noteEn: Depicts a sweet (甘) fruit in a tree (木). Based on the original meaning "plum", now written as 梅. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

囚.noteEn: Depicts a person (人) trapped inside an enclosure (囗).

於.noteEn: Originally a variant form of 烏 (crow). The current use as a function word is a phonetic loan.

厄.noteEn: Pictograph of a harness on a horse.

尭.noteEn: Depicts a mound of dirt (土) on top of a platorm (兀), representing the meaning "tall; lofty", later used to describe the legendary Emperor Yao.

串.noteEn: Pictograph of two objects on a skewer or strung together.

凸.noteEn: Pictograph of a bump sticking out. Opposite of 凹.

凹.noteEn: Pictograph of a concavity. Opposite of 凸.

斥.noteEn: Originally written as 㡿. Composed of 广 (roof) and 屰 (contrary; oppose). The purpose of the 广 component is unclear.

甫.noteEn: Pictograph of something sprouting (屮) from a field (田), depicting a garden or orchard, now written as 圃. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

只.noteEn: Origin unclear. In simplified Chinese 只 is also used to mean "[measure word]", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 隻.

丑.noteEn: Pictograph of an animal's paw. In simplified Chinese 丑 is also used to mean "ugly", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 醜.

戴.noteEn: Depicts a pair of hands (共) putting something on top of the head. The 𢦔 component represents the sound.

允.noteEn: Pictograph of a person nodding their head in agreement.

畏.noteEn: Pictograph of a ghost wielding a stick, which is a fearful sight to behold.

邑.noteEn: Pictograph of a person (卩) outside a city wall (囗). Appears as a component in the right side of characters as ⻏.

酉.noteEn: Pictograph of a container for wine.

乞.noteEn: Originally a variant of 气. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

且.noteEn: Originally a pictograph of a sacrificial altar. The current meaning "moreover" is a phonetic loan.

亦.noteEn: Pictograph of a person, with two dots at the armpits. Based on the original meaning "armpit", now written as 腋. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

勾.noteEn: 勾 is a component form of 句.

吏.noteEn: The characters 史 (history), 吏 (government official), 使 (cause; use; instruct), and 事 (matter; work; affair) are all etymologically related and all derive from the same ancient character, depicting a hand (又) holding some object. There are various theories about theories about what this object is, including a writing utensil, a container for official documents, a flag, or a hunting tool. These four characters were originally all written the same, but later marks were added to distinguish them.

弄.noteEn: Depicts a pair of hands (廾) playing with a jade object (玉).

旦.noteEn: Pictograph of the sun rising above the horizon.

朕.noteEn: Originally depicted two hands (廾) holding an object (丨) to patch up a hole in a boat (舟), representing the meaning "seam; crack". Since cracks in bones were used for fortune-telling in ancient China, the meaning shifted later to "omen; sign" and "sovereign".

采.noteEn: Pictograph of a hand (爪) picking fruit from a tree (木).
